summary: Figure F2_static_asr illustrates the performance of different spotlighting variants under a theoretical framework. The bars represent the estimated proportion p̂_τ, while the whiskers show the Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals. The triangles indicate the one-sided upper bound p̄_τ. The data shows that as the number of successes (s) decreases, the upper bound p̄_τ also decreases, indicating tighter control over the risk.
observations: The variant 'none' has the highest p̂_τ at 0.4275 with the widest confidence interval.
The variant 'datamark_dynamic' has the lowest p̂_τ at 0.1000 and the narrowest upper bound p̄_τ at 0.12818.
The variant 'random_scramble' has the lowest p̂_τ at 0.0650 and the narrowest upper bound p̄_τ at 0.08905.
The variant 'base64' has a p̂_τ of 0.1525 and an upper bound p̄_τ of 0.18523, showing moderate performance.
caveats: The data is in theory-mode and simulated, so the results are not based on actual experimental data.
The sample sizes for s are small, which may affect the reliability of the confidence intervals.
